newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares tumble in late electronic trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares tumble in late electronic trade.

text.p: German shares tumbled nearly 1.60 percent in late electronic trade on Friday after a sharp fall in the Dow Jones Industrial index scuppered positive sentiment on the German share market.
The market at one point rose over half a percent in afternoon trade, supported by the ongoing rise of the dollar to above 1.86 marks and early firmness on the Dow Jones Industrial index.
This changed after data from the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM), suggesting that the strong U.S. economy was starting to slow, dealt U.S. stocks a crippling blow in late trade.
The IBIS DAX index of 30 German blue chips ended down 68.54 points at 4,336.98 points, conclusively breaching support at 4,400 points which had held for most of the day.
Daimler was one of the focuses of attention over the day as the share fell after U.S. investment banks Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgraded 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Daimler.
Merrill also cut Daimler to intermediate reduce from neutral but left the share as a long-term hold.
The downgrades came after Daimler released six-month figures that showed group operating profit more than doubling to 1.849 billion marks.
Daimler CEO Juergen Schrempp said he did not understand the disappointment among analysts, and described on Friday in a radio interview the company's performance as "excellent".
Shares in Daimler ended 3.11 percent lower at 148.10 marks.
The other big corporate news of the afternoon was the announcement that German software group SAP AG was planning a hook-up with U.S. giant Intel to form an Internet joint venture.
SAP shares rose early on, but were ultimately unable to shake off the influence of the U.S. and the shaer ended down 8.80 marks at 439.20.
U.S. payroll data brought the market lower initially but the market righted itself for a time afterwards.
U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 316,000 in July, above the forecast, and June personal income rose 0.6 percent, also above forecast.

For next week dealers said they were looking ahead to first-half figures from Adidas AG, Veba AG and Schering, as well as German unemployment data from Nuremberg on Wednesday and German industrial orders data.
